plain_english_policy: This bill authorizes Alabama county commissions to initiate a local referendum asking voters if they want an additional gasoline tax of up to $0.05 per gallon. If approved by voters, the collected funds must be used exclusively for maintaining, improving, replacing, or constructing specific county roads and bridges listed in advance on a 'project list.' The tax is limited to five years unless renewed via another referendum. Funds cannot pay employee salaries or buy equipment; they can only cover project costs (materials up to 20% may go toward materials used by county workers). Projects must meet state design standards based on traffic volume.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would create a new, optional local funding mechanism for rural and small-town infrastructure. It shifts some road maintenance financial responsibility from the state or general county funds to specific voters in counties that choose this option. The policy direction is toward localized control over transportation spending with strict transparency requirements (public posting of project lists) and usage restrictions ensuring tax dollars go directly to physical assets rather than operational expenses like payroll.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives Ford and Hammett advanced this bill, indicating support for expanding local options for county road funding through a targeted gasoline tax.
evidence_quotes: This bill would allow a county commission to call for a local referendum to authorize the county commission to levy an excise tax on gasoline or motor fuel not to exceed five cents ($.05) per gallon for specific county road and bridge projects identified by the county prior to the referendum.

The proceeds of any taxes imposed under authority of this act shall be deposited into a special county road and bridge safety fund to be expended for the maintenance, improvement, replacement, and construction of county-maintained roads and bridges.
